questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Smartphone addiction and how to use phones less
The history of the smartphone
How to make videos for YouTube
Why teenagers need their own phones from a young age
questions.why: They discuss smartphone addiction and ideas like app timers to help us use phones less.

questions.q: What causes the confusion at the start?
options: Catherine doesn't own a smartphone
Rob forgot his phone
Catherine uses her phone 18 or 19 hours a day
Rob thinks Catherine means per month, not per week
questions.why: Rob thinks she means 18 or 19 hours a week, but Catherine says she meant a day.

questions.q: Why does Catherine keep checking her phone?
options: She is waiting for an important call
She is afraid of missing something interesting
Her boss sends her messages
She is playing a game
questions.why: She says she suffers from FOMO: something cool might be happening and she wants to catch it.

questions.q: What does Rob demonstrate while Catherine is looking at her phone?
options: How to switch a phone off
How to take a photo
How to set a timer on an app to limit your phone use
That she ignores him because of her phone
questions.why: Rob has to repeat 'Hello… I said…' and 'Catherine!' because she isn't listening, like a phubber.

questions.q: According to one survey, how many teenagers in the USA feel addicted to their phones?
options: About a quarter
About half
Almost all
About one in ten
questions.why: Rob says half of teenagers in the USA feel like they are addicted to their mobile phones.

questions.q: What danger of phones does psychologist Jean Twenge mention?
options: We lose track of time and an hour passes
Our eyes get tired
We spend too much money on games and other apps
We sleep badly at night
questions.why: She talks about getting into social media and 'realising that an hour has passed'.

questions.q: What does Catherine say happens to her with online videos?
options: She never watches them
She only watches BBC videos
She gets lost watching one video after another
She watches them to fall asleep
questions.why: She says 'I've spent ages just getting lost in video after video.'

questions.q: What does Jean Twenge think about app timers?
options: They are a waste of time
They will make people even more addicted to their phones
Nobody will use them
She seems to like them, as people would meet more
questions.why: Catherine says she doesn't say so directly, but seems to think it's good because people would meet in person.
